_source: 2026-09-07. UI sfx pool = FDOTHER.DAT resource #31 (nested LLLLLL, 14 sub-samples), used as table_ptr [0x53eec] by play_sfx_a (0x25a96) / play_sfx_b (0x25b45).
_method: No listening involved. Each index is judged from three independent sources: (a) the enclosing function of its play_sfx call site, decompiled and cross-referenced against functions this project had already named elsewhere; (b) measured properties of the corresponding raw 8-bit PCM sample, re-extracted from FDOTHER.DAT this round rather than reusing the deleted remake/assets copy; (c) how often / at what moment the call site fires. This is the same shape of argument that upgraded index 0 to CONFIRMED.
_waveform_measurements: re-measured 2026-09-07 at the documented 11025Hz assumption; columns are bytes, ms, min, max, peak-to-peak, RMS about 128, and the share of samples within +/-2 of the 128 silence centre
_correction_to_doc36: doc36's sub-sample table calls #5/#6 '幾乎全 0x80 (近似靜音段)'. Measured, they are rms 5.18 / 3.95 with peak-to-peak 40 / 32 -- quiet, but the same order as #0 (p2p 32, rms 9.16), not near-silence. 'Low amplitude' is accurate; 'nearly silent' overstates it.

2.enclosing: UI main-loop animation tick: increments a counter, advances a 0..3 frame cycle every 2nd call, redraws (FUN_00016559), plays sfx on EVERY call; both callers (0x16139, 0x164a2) are inside FUN_00015f84, the core UI routine every town/church/shop loop calls
2.argument: fires every tick, so a loud sample would be a continuous racket; it measures as one of the shortest and quietest in the pool

3.enclosing: death handler: scans every unit for record[+5]&1 == 0 (not yet flagged dead) AND HP-current (record+0x40) == 0, runs a 13-frame animation, then sets record[+5] = 1
3.argument: longest sample in the pool and among the widest dynamic range; cross-checks with the 2026-09-07 revival work, which independently established record[+5]&1 = dead and that revival clears it and restores HP

4.enclosing: 0x1A30B, the turn orchestrator doc11 documents as the single destination of all three end-turn entries

5.enclosing: unit info / status card display (the same routine church service 0 calls after picking a member); this site is preceded by 0x4e8af taking a string pointer
5.semantics: text/message shown inside the info card (unconfirmed which half)
5.confidence: MEDIUM -- 5 and 6 are byte-identical in length and both low amplitude, which suggests a paired open/close or show/hide, but the pairing direction is not established

6.semantics: the other half of the same pair

7.enclosing: field cursor/confirm handler -- doc11 records that this function calls the 0x16F55 system ring when there is no actionable friendly unit under the cursor; sfx 7 plays on the branch where a bit test FAILS
7.argument: exactly the same length as index 0 (the soft cursor blip) but roughly 3x the RMS and zero silence -- a short, harsh, dense click, which is the shape a refusal buzzer has and a cursor tick does not

8.enclosing: ring key-reading routine (doc11 lists 0x1741C/0x177FC as the readers for the 0x16F55 system ring); the site follows setting four dwords to 0x390

11.call_site: 0x2cac3 in an un-boundaried function starting 0x2c67d (recovered with tools/find_enclosing_function.py; Ghidra has no boundary there, so no decompile)
11.confidence: LOW -- a 221ms sample on a 1-in-9 cadence does not obviously fit a tick; the enclosing function still needs to be decompiled
